title: pr-5890-review-scratchpad-ryan-cho
summary: Scratchpad for PR #5890 (dataset cache + batching refactor). Working notes, checklist, perf numbers, and follow-ups. Mostly personal; share once tidy.
review_checklist: Read PR description + linked design doc (ensure goals match: reduce duplicate decoding work, improve batching headroom)
Confirm backward compatibility for existing cache keys (format/version bump?)
Verify locking semantics around cache population (race conditions on concurrent warmups)
Check metrics emitted: cache_hits, cache_misses, cache_evictions, avg_batch_latency
Confirm unit & integration tests cover cold/warm cache and concurrent requests
Look for unsafe pointer/shared-mutable usage in C++ runtime paths
Validate config knobs: max_cache_entries, entry_ttl, enable_prefix_caching (defaults sane)
Review rollout plan: canary on dedicated pool -> gradually increase -> fallback path if regressions
code_comments: runtime/cache/dataset_cache.h: consider adding explicit version field rather than embedding in key string (easier migration)
runtime/cache/dataset_cache.cpp L243: potential double-lock if background evictor runs during insert; prefer scoped_lock + try_lock pattern
serve/batcher.cc: batching window uses system_clock::now() repeatedly - use a single timestamp per batch to avoid jitter affecting ordering
python/tests/test_cache_integration.py: test uses time.sleep(0.1) for timing - unstable on CI; replace with fake time or wait-for-metric pattern
quantization/quant_utils.py: docstring typo; not critical but fix for readability
perf: microbenchmark shows 12% win on p3.2xlarge for throughput with new cache, but 8% latency regression at p99 under 128 concurrent streams - need root cause
local_test_results: Local perf (n=5): baseline throughput 410 tok/s -> new cache 459 tok/s (+11.9%), median latency unchanged, p99 +8%
Unit tests: all pass locally (pytest -q) except test_concurrent_eviction flakiness on first run; increased seed stability fixes intermittently
Integration: deployed to staging-dedicated, smoke OK, observed ~30% cache hit rate for sample workload (expected ~45%)
Memory: resident set increased by ~40MB per worker due to caching of prefix slices; need to verify eviction pressure on small instances
open_questions: Why is cache hit rate lower in staging than the offline trace? Is key normalization different in the router?
Should we add optional metrics tagging by model_id to see per-model hit rates? Might increase cardinality but useful for debugging
Is current TTL semantics OK (sliding vs fixed)? Design doc suggests sliding but code implements fixed - intentional?
Do we need explicit migration tooling for cache key format change? (script to invalidate old keys vs bump namespace)
follow_ups: Add a migration plan to the PR description (invalidate old namespace + note for Dedicated customers)
Replace sleeps in tests with a deterministic time fixture (tracked in JIRA-1128)
Add canary rollout steps to the runbook: start at 5% on low-traffic pool, validate p99 for 24h, increase to 25%
Instrument per-model cache metrics (create a lightweight label, monitor cardinality) - spike discussion with observability team
Schedule pairing session with Samir to dig into p99 latency regression on high concurrency
If memory delta is significant, consider configurable max_cached_prefix_bytes per worker
notes_to_self: Don't block merge just for test flakes if mitigations (deterministic time) are in PR; prefer fast follow-up. Remember to update the changelog entry and add a short blurb for release notes highlighting 'reduced duplicate decoding and improved throughput with configurable cache'
next_steps: Push small fixes: test flake fix + docstring typo
Ask author to add migration notes and canary plan
Run focused p99 stress tests on 128/256 concurrent streams with and without cache enabled
Draft short Slack post for #eng-serving-runtime summarizing expected impact and asking for early canary volunteers
raw_notes: -- scribbles from review session 2026-02-26: noticed dataset_cache keys include request_id in some paths -> probably accidental flattening in router layer; talk to console team. Also, check that batcher preserves request order for prefix caching to be effective. If we can't guarantee ordering, prefix caching may be less helpful for chat-like workloads.
